bottom_line: Tofersen — VALOR. Stated failure: Phase III: 28-week clinical primary endpoint missed; later biomarker-based regulatory pathway. Diagnosis (claim 1.3, supported): VALOR missed its primary endpoint: the LS mean difference in ALSFRS-R change was 1.2 (95% CI -3.19 to 5.53; p=0.9689), indicating no statistically significant treatment effect.

(section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: post hoc; evidence strength: strong; check: hypothesis-generating).

(section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: post hoc; evidence strength: strong; check: hypothesis-generating).

(section: Candidate Responder Population; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: prespecified; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[10] VALOR missed the short-duration clinical primary endpoint. (section: Candidate Responder Population; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[11] Tofersen produced biomarker changes: CSF total SOD1 protein concentration ratio to baseline difference in LS geometric mean ratio 0.62 (95% CI 0.49 to 0.78, p<0.0001) and plasma NfL concentration ratio to baseline difference 0.33 (95% CI 0.25 to 0.45, p<0.0001) at Week 28. (section: Candidate Responder Population; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: prespecified; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

(section: Candidate Responder Population; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[13] VALOR (Part C) (NCT02623699) tested tofersen in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. (section: Related Indications; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[14] VALOR (Part C) (NCT02623699) studies Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis and tests TOFERSEN. (section: Related Indications; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[15] VALOR Part C missed its short-duration clinical primary endpoint: change from baseline in ALSFRS-R total score at Week 28 (Day 197), with an LS mean difference of 1.2 (95% CI -3.19 to 5.53; p=0.9689). (section: Evidence-Supported Redesign Options; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[16] Tofersen produced biomarker changes: CSF total SOD1 protein concentration ratio to baseline was 0.62 (95% CI 0.49-0.78, p<0.0001) and plasma NfL concentration ratio to baseline was 0.33 (95% CI 0.25-0.45, p<0.0001) at Week 28, indicating target engagement and downstream biological effect. (section: Evidence-Supported Redesign Options; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[17] After the VALOR primary endpoint failure, the development strategy pivoted to pursue accelerated approval using plasma neurofilament light as a surrogate, alongside further testing; FDA granted accelerated approval in April 2023 for SOD1-ALS, which is a biomarker/regulatory strategy and not proof that post hoc clinical analysis made the original primary result positive. (section: Evidence-Supported Redesign Options; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[18] Patients with SOD1-ALS might still benefit, as the post-failure strategy and accelerated approval were specifically for SOD1-ALS, supported by biomarker reductions (NfL and SOD1) and longer follow-up providing additional biological and clinical context. (section: Evidence-Supported Redesign Options; sources: curated record, ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: curated, registry; evidence status: hypothesis-generating; evidence strength: strong; check: hypothesis-generating).
question: Why did tofersen miss its VALOR primary endpoint, and which patients might still benefit?
raw: VALOR Part C missed its prespecified Week 28 ALSFRS-R primary endpoint (LS mean difference 1.2; 95% CI -3.19 to 5.53; p=0.9689) [3,9,15], showing no statistically significant clinical benefit. Secondary biomarker changes—CSF total SOD1 ratio 0.62 and plasma NfL ratio 0.33 at Week 28 [6,8,11,16]—supported target engagement but are hypothesis-generating post hoc results. The curated record notes FDA accelerated approval in April 2023 for SOD1-ALS using plasma NfL as a surrogate [4,5,8,12,17], a biomarker/regulatory strategy rather than proof that post hoc clinical analysis reversed the primary failure. Lines do not show which baseline characteristics predict response; patients with SOD1-ALS might still benefit [18], but this remains hypothesis-generating.
